blocks.text: Chrome on Mac is the browser you already know. The difference is how you set it up for purchasing work. Most days that means supplier portals, approval emails, saved logins and a lot of open tabs. This page covers the Chrome settings that help with that work. Public sources do not describe how procurement teams use Chrome day to day, so any procurement example here is an illustration, not a measured habit.
What Chrome on Mac already gives you for purchasing work

Google's Chrome page names three features worth using at work. Google Password Manager is built in, and it autofills addresses and passwords. Tab groups let you sort open tabs into named sets. The page names both Windows and Mac. It does not list Mac-only features, so the settings below apply to any Mac that runs a supported version.

Repetitive work adds up. A 2026 survey by Sapio Research for Ivalua asked 1,000 procurement decision-makers and CIOs in the UK, US, Germany and France. Procurement teams said they spend about 18% of working time on manual tasks that AI could handle. The same research puts the loss at about £1.14 million a year across businesses. Treat this as one industry vendor's survey, not an independent study. It still shows why small Chrome habits matter.
Update Chrome before you open a supplier portal

Start with the version number. Chrome checks for updates from the More button, the dots icon at the top right of the window. Go to More > Help > About Google Chrome. Your version number appears under the Google Chrome heading. Relaunch Chrome when it asks you to.

Chrome needs macOS 13 Ventura or later, according to Google's update help page. If your Mac runs an older system, Chrome will not reach the current version. Check your macOS version first, through the Apple menu > About This Mac, before you blame a portal for a broken page.

Chrome can also keep itself current for every user on the Mac. This works when Chrome sits in the Applications folder. Use the Automatically update Chrome for all users button on the About Google Chrome page. If your IT team manages this Mac, ask them before you change the setting.

items: Open Chrome and click More, the dots icon at the top right.
Go to Help > About Google Chrome.
Read the version number under the Google Chrome heading.
Wait for the update to finish, then relaunch Chrome when it asks.
If Chrome sits in Applications and you manage the Mac yourself, turn on automatic updates for all users.

blocks.title: Check the Mac first
blocks.text: Chrome needs macOS 13 Ventura or later. Check your macOS version before you chase a Chrome update that will not install.
Use tab groups to keep each supplier or project together

Tab groups stop your window from turning into a wall of tabs. Right-click a tab and choose Add tab to group. Then pick New group or an existing group. You can also drag a tab onto a group that already exists. Right-click the colored circle or the name of a group to rename it or change its color.

Here is a simple pattern. Make one group for each supplier portal. Put the purchase order page, the invoice page and the shared folder in the same group. When the work for that supplier is done, collapse the group. Your window stays readable, and the tabs stay where you left them.

Tab groups can sync. If you sign in to Chrome with a Google Account and sync history and tabs, changes to tab groups save and sync across all your devices. Check this on your own setup. Third-party guides disagree about phone sync, and Google's help page does not settle that question.
Google Password Manager and the screen lock setting

Open More > Passwords and autofill > Google Password Manager. Select a site to see its saved login, then click Show password to reveal it. When a site has one saved login, Chrome fills the sign-in form for you. When you have several logins for one site, click the username field and pick the one you need.

Here is the setting most people miss. On Mac, the option Use your screen lock when filling passwords makes Chrome ask for your Mac screen lock before it fills or reveals a password. It is off by default. Turn it on if the Mac is shared or if you work in public places. The cost is a screen lock prompt each time Chrome fills a password.

blocks.text: Offer to save passwords and passkeys sits on the same settings page. On a shared Mac, turn it off, so Chrome does not store new logins there. On your own Mac, leave it on if the convenience helps. Either way, check the page again after each major Chrome update.
Use a private window for one-off sign-ins

Press ⌘⇧N to open an Incognito window. Use it for a one-off login on a machine you share, or for an account that is not yours. Google's Incognito help page explains what the window does and does not keep. Read it before you rely on the window for anything sensitive.
A worked example: chasing a missing invoice in a supplier portal

Say a supplier portal shows an invoice as pending, but your email says it was sent. Open the portal in its own tab group. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur what pending means on that page. Lazur reads the status text and explains it in plain words. Then ask Lazur to draft a short reply that asks for a resend.

Read the draft before you send it. Change the names, dates and invoice references to match your records. Send the reply from your own mail app. Keep the portal and your mail in separate groups, so the reply does not get lost among other tabs. Lazur explains the status, but your team's rules still decide the next step.
Troubleshooting a supplier page that will not load in Chrome

items: Check the Chrome version under More > Help > About Google Chrome.
Check that macOS is 13 Ventura or later.
Reload the page with ⌘R.
Open the same page in an Incognito window with ⌘⇧N. If it loads there, a saved setting may be the cause.

blocks.text: If the page still fails, stop retrying. Copy the exact error message and the time it appeared. Send both to the supplier's support team. A clear report gets a faster answer than another round of reloads.
Setting up a new Mac for purchasing work

Set up the Mac before your first live purchase, not during it. Install Chrome and sign in with your work Google Account. Turn on sync for history and tabs. Turn on the screen lock option for saved passwords. Then set up a tab group for each recurring supplier. A short setup session saves a lot of hunting later.
Where Lazur fits while you work in Chrome

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click before it goes on.
Ask Lazur about a supplier page, not just a menu

Lazur is most useful on pages with unfamiliar words. Hold ⌥ ⌘ on a page that says goods receipt or pending approval, and ask what it means. Lazur explains the term from what is on screen. It cannot know your company's approval rules, so check those with your own team.
What Lazur will not do in Chrome

Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app. It has no partnership with any app maker. Expect it to point, explain, draft and talk you through each step. You do the clicking, which is slower on a long form, but it keeps you in control of what gets submitted.

Lazur can draft messages to suppliers. Ask for a short, polite reply, and read the result before you send it. To write your own words instead, hold fn to dictate clean text at the cursor in any app. Dictation is included, and it is unlimited on both paid plans.
Research suppliers in Lazur's own Chrome tabs

For background research, ask Lazur to run the job. Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. Use it for a first pass on a supplier's public information. Check any figure in the report against the supplier's own pages before you rely on it.
Privacy: what Lazur sees and where audio goes

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so Lazur can answer. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Check the current privacy details before you use Lazur on a screen with bank details or personal data.
Common mistakes with Chrome on a purchasing Mac

items: Running an old Chrome version, then blaming the supplier portal.
Saving logins on a shared Mac with the screen lock option off.
Keeping every supplier in one long row of tabs with no groups.
Assuming tab groups sync to a phone without checking your own setup.
Expecting Lazur to click through a form. Lazur guides, and you click.
Sending a drafted message without reading it first.

blocks.text: Keyboard shortcuts that save time in Chrome on Mac

items: ⌘T opens a new tab.
⌘W closes the current tab.
⌘⇧T reopens the last tab you closed.
⌘L puts the cursor in the address bar.
⌘F searches the current page.
⌘⌥← and ⌘⌥→ move between tabs.
⌘⇧N opens an Incognito window.

blocks.text: Pair these shortcuts with tab groups, and you spend less time hunting for a tab. When you cannot find a button, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur to point at it. Lazur draws the circle, and you make the click.
Next steps you can take today

items: Check your Chrome version under More > Help > About Google Chrome.
Turn on the screen lock option in Google Password Manager settings if the Mac is shared.
Set up a tab group for each supplier or project you handle most.
Try Lazur on a Chrome page you do not understand. Start from the download page.

blocks.text: If your purchasing work also runs through Gmail or Google Sheets, these guides cover the same Chrome setup: [how to create a label in Gmail](/how-to/create-a-label-in-gmail), [how to sort data by column in Google Sheets](/how-to/sort-data-by-column-in-google-sheets), and [how to unsubscribe from emails in Gmail](/how-to/unsubscribe-from-emails-in-gmail). For the Chrome side of Lazur, see [Lazur for Chrome on Mac](/apps/chrome).
What the survey numbers do and do not show

The 18% figure and the £1.14 million estimate come from one survey run by an industry vendor, Ivalua, with Sapio Research. Use them as a reason to look at your own time. Do not treat them as a benchmark for your team. The Smartsheet figure has no stated sample size or year. Read it as a rough signal, not a measurement.
Pricing and the free trial

Lazur offers a free trial with no credit card. The trial starts when you first open the app. Dictation is unlimited on both paid plans. Plan limits and prices change over time, so check the [pricing page](/pricing) before you choose a plan.

faq.question: Which Chrome version do I need on a Mac?
faq.answer: Chrome needs macOS 13 Ventura or later, according to Google's update help page. Check your Chrome version under More > Help > About Google Chrome. The sources do not name a current Chrome version number, so confirm it on your own Mac.

faq.question: Where is the screen lock setting for Google Password Manager on Mac?
faq.answer: Open More > Passwords and autofill > Google Password Manager, then open its settings. Turn on Use your screen lock when filling passwords if the Mac is shared. The option is off by default.

faq.question: Do Chrome tab groups sync between my Mac and other devices?
faq.answer: Google says changes to tab groups sync across devices when you sign in with a Google Account and sync history and tabs. Check this on your own setup. Sources disagree about phone sync, so test it before you rely on it.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons in a supplier portal for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It points, explains, drafts and guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: Is it safe to use Lazur on a screen with bank details?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Check the current privacy details before you use it on sensitive screens.
